messages:
jamie: quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA RFC — saw a sharp p99 regress when the grouped-query kernel picks the 'short-prefix' codepath for some multi-query workloads. any thoughts?

sam: can you paste a repro or logs? which model + seq len? :thinking:

jamie: reproducer attached in thread, running bloom-560m, seq=1024, avg request has 6 grouped queries. p99 jumps from 95ms -> 260ms after kernel switch. here's the relevant slice of logs:
```
[2026-03-19T14:02:01Z] kernel_selector: picked=mqa_grouped_v2 reason=kv_cache_hit pct=0.87
[2026-03-19T14:02:01Z] runtime_batch: size=8 latency_ms=24
[2026-03-19T14:02:01Z] attention_kernel: launch=grouped_query_short_prefix latency_ms=210
```

rachel: that launch latency screams mismatch between expected prefix distribution and the optimized kernel's kernel-local memory usage. v2 assumed prefixes <128 tokens packed, but when KV cache exists and queries are scattered, memory copies spike.

mike: hmm, do we have telemetry for per-kernel memory copy time? I thought we only had end-to-end latencies.

anika: we do emit kernel micrometrics but they live behind a different trace flag. we can enable for the next run. my concern: selector heuristics are currently only based on seq_len and batch_size. no cache-fragmentation signal.

jamie: exact. proposal: add a 'kv_fragmentation' estimator that approximates how many distinct KV slices a grouped-query will access, and feed that into the cost model. cheap to compute at select time.

sam: how would kv_fragmentation be computed cheaply? walking KV sets sounds expensive.

anika: heuristic: count unique attention_start positions across queries in the grouped request, normalized by avg_query_len. essentially (#unique_starts / avg_len). cheap since query metadata already present.

rachel: sounds reasonable. also consider a penalty term for kernel-local copy when unique_starts > N_threshold. that will discourage short-prefix kernel for highly-fragmented workloads.

mike: alternative: keep current selector but add a fast fallback probe — run one token with chosen kernel, measure per-token kernel_time_est, and if it's above threshold, switch to generic kernel for the rest of the request. downsides: extra latency for first token and added complexity.

jamie: probe idea is neat but risky for high-QPS; the probe itself might amplify P99. i prefer a predictive selector + sampled telemetry to refine model.

anika: agree. plan suggestion: 1) add kv_fragmentation estimate to selector (cheap), 2) enable micrometrics in canary (ci-bot will flip flag), 3) run workload sweep to fit penalty term, 4) ship soft rollout with canary weight 5%.

sam: +1 for canary. what about API/interface changes — do we need to change kernel selector API signature?

anika: minimal change: add optional metadata field `kv_fragmentation` to GroupedQueryDescriptor. defaults to 0 if missing, so old clients unaffected. selector implementations read it if present. example proto snippet:
```proto
message GroupedQueryDescriptor {
  repeated Query queries = 1;
  float kv_fragmentation = 10; // optional, default 0 in codegen
}
```

rachel: love the backward-compatible approach. we should also add unit tests that simulate high fragmentation with small prefixes.

mike: can we add a guardrail to avoid oscillation? i.e., selector should avoid flipping kernels mid-request but also avoid flip-flopping across requests. maybe add sticky caching per-route for 20s.

jamie: sticky routing makes sense for stability. record chosen kernel per route+model for short TTL. helps with throughput stability during traffic spikes.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: enable-micrometrics-flag -> canary cluster. build #4529 queued.

anika: ok I'll draft the change and open an RFC follow-up PR with benchmarks and the new proto. assigning action items: anika write PR, sam run micrometrics sweep, rachel write unit tests, mike verify sticky cache behavior in load test, jamie coordinate canary rollout. anyone want to swap tasks? :thumbsup:

sam: I'll take the sweep.

rachel: tests on me.

mike: I'll prototype sticky cache TTL knob.

jamie: thanks all — aim to have canary running by end of week. if logs show anything unexpected ping here and @eng-runtime on urgent.

anika: saving links to notes and repro in the RFC thread. will tag when PR's up.
